evidence.s1_ci: ci.yml runs `npm ci`, `npm test` and `npm run build` in site/ on `pull_request` (step1.patch 35-64). All three scripts exist in site/package.json:14-16, which is the only package.json in the repo. Permissions are least privilege: ci `contents: read`; pages has `contents: read` at the top and `pages: write`/`id-token: write` only on the deploy job (115-117); release has `contents: write`. Only `github.token` is used, there is no `pull_request_target`, and nothing was run or pushed. pages.yml deploys on `push: branches: [main]` plus `workflow_dispatch`. A manual dispatch can pick any branch, but the default github-pages environment rules usually block that. PAGES_BASE is read by the baseline site/vite.config.ts:11. The main failure is that no action is pinned to a commit SHA: `actions/checkout@v7`, `actions/setup-node@v7`, `actions/upload-pages-artifact@v5`, `actions/deploy-pages@v5` (step1.patch 54-55, 98-99, 107, 123, 148-149) all use mutable tags.
evidence.s1_readme: README (step1.patch 299-368) has sections for Requirements (Node 22), Install (`cd site && npm ci`), Develop (`npm run dev`, `npm run preview`), Test (`npm test`), Build (`npm run build` and PAGES_BASE), Contribute data (family directories match FAMILIES in site/scripts/records.mjs:13, fixtures/profiles exists, issue templates exist), Versions and releases, and License (MIT, matches LICENSE:3). Every command it shows exists in site/package.json:9-17.
evidence.s1_release: There is one strategy. The version is kept in site/package.json `version` (0.1.0). A release is made by pushing a `v*` tag, and release.yml checks that the tag equals package.json and that CHANGELOG has a matching `## [X.Y.Z]` section before it tests, builds and publishes with `gh release` (step1.patch 155-190). CHANGELOG.md states Keep a Changelog 1.1.0 and SemVer. CONTRIBUTING.md defines the meaning of major/minor/patch, the release steps and Conventional Commits with a type table. Dependabot covers npm in /site and github-actions, grouped weekly. All 8 commits in commits.txt follow the convention. One inconsistency: CONTRIBUTING assigns dependencies to `build`, but dependabot.yml uses the prefix `chore(deps)` for npm (step1.patch 14, 246, 253).
evidence.s2_requirements: Route: router.ts:34-43 handles `#/compare/<a>/<b>` from the hash, so it survives a reload. App.svelte renders Compare.svelte. Drawing: two `<path>` elements in one SVG with `role="img"` and `aria-label` 'Profiles of {a} and {b}' using record names (Compare.svelte:25-28), built from caseOuterProfile in a single viewportFor (compare.ts outlines). Table: `<caption>` 'Dimensions (mm|in)', headers Symbol / name A / name B / Difference, FIELD_LABELS symbols, B−A, FIELD_UNITS and Tol fields excluded (compare.ts compareRows, orderedFields drops Tol). Units come from unitSystem(): metric uses formatValue, imperial uses displayNumber(…,'in'). Cartridge.svelte:360-369 adds a labelled 'Compare with' NativeSelect and a 'Compare' button that sets href.compare(key, chosen). German strings were added. Every listed requirement is met.
evidence.s2_correctness: Both profiles start at z=0 (the head face) in caseOuterProfile (case.ts:438ff, rimProfile at z 0). viewportFor([pA,pB]) gives one scale and a common zMin, and fullSectionPath mirrors each profile about r=0, so the shared axis and head alignment are correct. compareRows only takes plain numbers from the `cartridge` part, skips FIELD_UNITS fields (pressures, M, angles) and Tol fields, and uses FIELD_LABELS (e.g. 'e min', 'delta L'). Metric values use formatValue unrounded. Imperial values and differences use displayNumber, which divides by 25.4. The metric difference goes through displayNumber(…,'mm') (toPrecision(12)), which removes float noise such as 2.3000000000000007. That is a defensible reading of 'written the same way'. Shotshells are excluded from the select, and an unknown key or failed adaptMetallic shows an alert instead of crashing.
evidence.s2_fit: The feature reuses @lib/core (FIELD_LABELS, FIELD_UNITS, GROUP_ORDER, orderedFields, formatValue), @lib/geom (viewportFor, fullSectionPath), @lib/shapes2d (adaptMetallic, caseOuterProfile), site units.ts displayNumber, units.svelte unitSystem, PageHeader, NativeSelect and ShadcnButton. It follows the existing structure: site/src/lib/compare.ts next to router/metadata, routes/Compare.svelte, a lazy chunk in App.svelte, and an entry in metadata.ts. The diff is small and focused. Small deviations: a hard-coded colour `#d9480f` and inline `style=` legend spans in Compare.svelte:28-32 instead of theme tokens or classes.
evidence.s2_tests: compare.test.ts tests compareRows on the real 308_win and 300_win_mag records (e min/L1 present; Pmax, PK, M, angles and Tol absent), the shared-only rule, metric and imperial cells, and that outlines returns two distinct paths. router.test.ts adds round-trip and malformed-hash cases. All of this is in the existing Vitest setup (site/src/**). Gaps: the outlines test does not check head-face alignment, the common scale or the axis. Nothing covers the SVG accessible name, the table caption and headers, or the Compare with / Compare control on the detail page.
evidence.s3_fixes: Bug: compareRows now iterates over the union `{...y, ...x}` of both groups and handles a missing group, with `a`/`b` typed `number | null` (step3.patch 57-91). cells returns '' for an unpublished side and for the difference (93-109). New tests check delta L (308 only) and R3 (300 WM only) on the real records, plus empty cells. Style: the step-2 markup already right-aligned the two cartridge columns, Difference and their headers (`text-right` on th and td, Compare.svelte:40-42, 50-52), and utilities win over the `legacy` layer (shadcn.css:1), so no change was needed and none was made. The only other edits are the 'shared' wording in the lede and the empty message in EN and DE, which follow directly from the fix.
evidence.cross_step: Step 2 adds a changelog entry under `## [Unreleased]` / Added (step2.patch 9), and step 3 amends that same unreleased entry. That is correct for a feature not yet released under Keep a Changelog. The stated strategy bumps the version only at release time, so leaving 0.1.0 unchanged is consistent. Commits `feat: compare two cartridges at #/compare/<a>/<b>` and `fix: list dimensions only one cartridge publishes in the compare table` follow Conventional Commits. The code is typed consistently (`Record<keyof typeof en>` keeps EN/DE in sync, Route union and metadata Record updated), so the CI checks plausibly pass. I did not run them.

unmet_requirements: Step 1 / CI criterion: the GitHub Actions in ci.yml, pages.yml and release.yml are referenced by version tags (@v7, @v5), not pinned to full commit SHAs.
strengths: The compare view is built almost entirely from existing modules: lib/core field metadata, lib/geom viewport and section paths, lib/shapes2d profiles, site units and UI components. The diff is small and correct: profiles share one scale, one axis and the head face at z=0.

The release process is coherent and enforced: the version lives in one place (site/package.json), a tag-triggered workflow checks the tag against that version and the Keep a Changelog section, and CONTRIBUTING states the SemVer meaning and Conventional Commits, which every commit follows.
The step 3 bug fix is precise (union of fields, null cells, empty Difference) and is tested against the exact delta L / R3 case the reviewer named. The changelog entry is updated under Unreleased.
issues: None of the actions in the three workflows is pinned to a commit SHA (actions/checkout@v7, setup-node@v7, upload-pages-artifact@v5, deploy-pages@v5). In a repository that accepts outside pull requests, that is a supply-chain gap.

The feature tests do not check the drawing's head-face alignment or common scale, the SVG/table accessible names and headers, or the Compare with control on the detail page. The outlines test only checks that two different paths exist.

Small inconsistencies: Dependabot npm commits use `chore(deps)` while CONTRIBUTING assigns dependencies to `build`. Compare.svelte hard-codes `#d9480f` and uses inline styles for the legend instead of theme tokens.
review.verdict: The compare feature and the step 3 fix are correct, small, reuse the repository's libraries properly and follow the release and commit conventions that step 1 set up. The main gap before merging is that the workflow actions are not pinned to SHAs; the drawing and UI tests are also thinner than the rest.
